# Vanilla Enhanced 3.4.7 - carademono (VE4, the Texture Overhaul's first pack, shipped)

**Vanilla Enhanced** for Daggerfall Unity, by **carademono** (Nexus Mods,
Daggerfall Unity mod 273: https://www.nexusmods.com/daggerfallunity/mods/273).
It is Daggerfall's own textures remastered: the terrain's tile sets, the
nature flats, the city walls and the dungeons.

These files come from the mod's public source repository,
https://github.com/drcarademono/vanilla-enhanced, at commit
`c0c9041c101ba8b57feb93258dda7a37be1b9433` (2025-05-08, "HD dungeon textures,
snowless swamps and jungles"; the manifests' version 3.4.7).
`tools/vanillaEnhancedVendor.mjs` wrote every file here and under
`public/art/vanilla-enhanced/` from that commit. Run without `--write`, it
checks the committed tree against a clone, byte for byte.

Mac (Lattymoy) asked for it on 2026-10-05: "I want to implement the vanilla
enhanced textures". He chose "Bundle the files in the repo", approved the
Port-Doctrine exception that needs ("Approved and yes"), and said "Put it in
the codebase".

**Permission: [Mac: record carademono's permission - the author's own words, or
the link to them - here. Mac confirmed on 2026-10-05 that it was given
("Approved and yes", answering "Do you have carademono's permission to
redistribute the files?"). Masked Roads is credited to carademono & Kokey;
Kokey's word is not recorded either. The repository states no licence.]**

## The doctrine exception

Vanilla Enhanced repaints Daggerfall's own textures, so Port-Doctrine's
**A RENDER OF GAME DATA IS GAME DATA** rule covers it. Under that rule, VE3
had the player attach their own copy. Mac approved carrying it instead.
`bible/01-Overview/Port-Doctrine.md` records the exception and limits it to
`public/art/vanilla-enhanced/`. `test/doctrine.test.js` marks these rows
`derived` and fails if any other row carries that mark.

## What is here

Three of the repository's mods, each in its own directory under
`public/art/vanilla-enhanced/`:

| mod | directory | pictures |
|---|---|---|
| Vanilla Enhanced - Base | `base/` | the 1,246 PNGs its manifest names, byte for byte |
| Vanilla Enhanced - Masked Roads | `masked-roads/` | its own 9 PNGs, and 21 slices of its texture arrays (below) |
| Vanilla Enhanced - Snowless Swamps and Jungles | `snowless-swamps-and-jungles/` | the 160 PNGs its manifest names, byte for byte |

That is 1,436 pictures, 22.4 MB. Each picture is served under its asset
name, with the extension written in lower case.

Beside this README:

- `<title>.dfmod.json`: each mod's manifest, verbatim.
- `<directory>.files.json`: each directory's listing, generated by the tool.
  It lists every file, the repository path it is the bytes of, and its
  sha256. This listing is the authority `test/doctrine.test.js` reads for what
  may stand in that directory.
- `vanilla-enhanced.index.json`: the name index each mod registers in the
  texture-mod door with (`src/systems/vanillaEnhancedPack.js`). It has the
  shape `buildDfmodIndex` writes for an attached bundle, plus where each
  array's slices are served from.

### The texture arrays ship as PNGs

Each mod carries its terrain tile sets as BC7 `Texture2DArray`s
(`<archive>-TexArray`). The tool decodes every slice and looks for the
picture it was made from: first the mod's own record PNG, then the
repository's source picture for that slice. It carries a slice only when the
slice is within BC7's error of that picture: a mean channel error of at most
1.5, and no single channel off by more than 48. It then serves the slice from
the picture. Measured at the pinned commit:

- **Base:** all 616 slices of its 11 arrays are its own record PNGs. The
  worst is 0.82 mean and 34 on a single channel.
- **Snowless Swamps and Jungles:** all 112 slices of its 402 and 403 arrays
  are its own record PNGs.
- **Masked Roads:** of its 10 arrays of 56 slices, 533 slices are the Base's
  records pixel for pixel and 6 are its own record PNGs. The remaining 21 are
  road tiles (records 46, 47 and 55) that no PNG it ships draws. Those are
  carried as `<archive>-TexArray_<slice>.png`, byte for byte from the
  repository's source pictures (`Textures/Terrain - Masked Roads/`). The
  closest a road tile comes to the Base record it replaces is 5.20 mean and
  78 on a single channel. The tolerance sits in that gap.
- **Masked Roads' 403 array is 57 slices deep.** Daggerfall Unity refuses an
  array whose depth is not the archive's (`TextureReplacement.cs:343`), so it
  is indexed with its depth and no slices. The door refuses it as DFU does.

Each listing's `Proofs` field records every slice's measured error.

### Left out

- **Winter Tracks** (Hazelnut & carademono): Daggerfall Unity never reaches
  its 30 records while the Base's arrays dress the ground.
  `TryImportTextureArray` takes the first mod that carries either name, and
  the Base carries both.
- **Kokey's Temperate**: Kokey's own mod, not part of the family.
- **Every mod's Materials** (`.mat`): the port has no Material reader
  (Ledger C, A MOD'S MATERIALS).

## How the port wears it

The three mods are mods, not the port's own art, and Daggerfall Unity reads
them as mods. They are behind Replace Game Artwork, read after the loose
folder, and loaded in the order their manifests' dependencies make. So they
register in the texture-mod door (`src/systems/dfmodTextures.js`
`setShippedDfmods`) beside any mod the player attaches, in one load order and
one lookup walk. The only difference is where a picture comes from: the
port's own file, fetched when it is first drawn.

- The Base is on by default (AUDIT VE; Mac: "Ensure this is on by default"),
  as a mod in Daggerfall Unity's Mods folder is; its add-ons are off until
  picked. The player's choice either way is kept on the prefs shelf as
  `dfmodShipped`.
- The pictures are decoded in a worker (AUDIT VE P1), as an attached bundle's
  are in its own.
- The Texture Overhaul card wears Vanilla Enhanced: the Base, plus the add-ons
  the player picks on the card.
- A copy the player attaches under the same name (a newer version from Nexus)
  shadows the shipped one.

See `bible/07-Rendering/Vanilla-Enhanced.md`.
